q: The Kalman decomposition for a linear system (A,B,C) decomposes the state space into four subspaces based on reachability and observability. The transfer function G(s) = C(sI−A)⁻¹B is determined entirely by:
opts: Only the reachable AND observable subspace (the 'good' part of the decomposition)
exp: Kalman decomposition: the transfer function G(s) depends only on the states that are both reachable and observable. Unreachable and/or unobservable modes are 'hidden' from the input-output description. A minimal realization (least-order state space representation) consists exactly of the reachable+observable subspace.
